messages.subject: Difficulty with simple univariate boxplot
messages.body_plain:
Dear all, From the Deducer menu I'm attempting to produce univariate boxplots for 3 continuous variables using Plot -> Interactive -> Box-plot (wide).  Two of these variables result in the expected plots [as confirmed by the base command boxplot()]
The above menu sequence equates to a call to ibox as follows:
ibox(births[,c("gestwks")]).
The result is very odd - I see the outer leaves of the boxplot (connected by a straight line) but no central box and no evidence of any outliers.  A summary of the variable shows that there are 10 missing values.
summary(births$gestwks)
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.    NA's
  24.69   37.94   39.12   38.72   40.09   43.16   10.00

Neither of the other variables have missing values - is that the issue?  Although the Plot -> Interactive -> Histogram plots OK and confirms that the distribution is highly negatively skewed.
Any ideas as to what the problem is and how to get around it?

messages.subject: SPSS variable labels
messages.body_plain:
Hey, I've used Deducer off an on for a while.  One problem I have that
keeps me from using it as much as I'd like is that most of the
datasets I work with come from SPSS.  The SPSS value labels are easily
viewable in the Deducer GUI.  However, the SPSS variable labels do not
appear.  Sometimes it is clear what the data is from the variable
name, but sometimes I have datasets with uninformative variable names
(v1, v2, etc).  So I have to either open up the data in SPSS to view
the variable labels, or go into the command line and check the label
attribute of each variable. e.g.:

attributes(mydataset$myvariable)$label

It would be useful to be able to add additional attributes of the
variables (in my case, label) to the variable view in Deducer.  Is
there already some way to do this and I'm just missing it?

Hi Marlon,

First the bad news,... JGR/Deducer does not provide a way to import
excel data files. you need to first save as a cvs, and then load them.

Next the good news,... This will change with the next release of JGR,
which will use the XLConnect package to bring in .xls and .xlsx files.
Those of you who know how to install the development version of JGR
can chack it out.

Ian

messages.subject: Re: Repeated measures / widget to select from a user-defined list
messages.subject_clean: Repeated measures / widget to select from a user-defined list
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Bill,

I'd be pleased to collaborate in your project; it would of course be
more efficient than duplicating efforts for similar ideas.

I had planned to use lm plus Anova from package 'car', plus a custom-
made wrapper to lht (linearHypotesis) to perform post-hoc paired (or
more complex) comparisons for main effects, as well as simple effects
or interaction contrasts. Since as far as I know, ezANOVA is based on
Anova, it wouldn't make a lot of difference, but I prefer the
flexibility of Anova to cope with customized models.

ezANOVA avoids the trouble of defining the between- and within-factor
formulas, but at the cost of only analysing full factorial models (as
far as I have managed to explore). For instance, if you analyse the
OBrienKaiser dataset (two between-subject factors --gender and
treatment--, plus two within-subject factors --phase and hour--),
ezANOVA lets me analyze a model whose formula would be
gender*treatment*phase*hour, but I have not been able to analyze
simpler models, for instance without higher order interactions --which
may be convenient in many cases.

I think that using Anova and allowing the user to customize the model
would be more inline with Deducer's tool for Linear Models. Anyway,
I'm open to discussion in this point. I'll contact you privately to
continue on commenting on this.

Helios

> The plotting only does 1 or 2 factors at a time at the moment, and the

> moment but you can take a look at all the source code here:

>
> --Bill

messages.subject: Minor bug: Paths with apostrophes
messages.body_plain:
A minor bug to put on the list:  When a user selects a file to open
and the path to that file contains an apostrophe (e.g., I have a
folder called "Bill's"), an error message is returned after the
command is executed, probably because R is interpreting the apostrophe
as the beginning of a quote.  A possible fix would be to gsub the path
name, replacing any apostrophe with an apostrophe preceded by an
escape character.
